supplies: definitions the part uses and does not carry

provenance.origin: 62 FR 63756 (FTC Enforcement Policy Statement on U.S. Origin Claims, 2 Dec 1997)
provenance.reviewed_by: Ihor Kvasha — read against the official FR PDF at 63768, 6 Sep 2026. The review caught a defect: the first extraction silently dropped the footnote marker after 'significant parts', and footnote 112 is definitional, not decorative. Marker restored and the footnote recorded as its own entry.
provenance.note: This overlay does NOT make § 323.2 resolvable. The part states its three-limb test, defines none of the terms, and cites neither this document nor 62 FR 63756 anywhere in its text. The overlay records where the content actually lives so a reader can follow it; the regulation's silence is the finding and the edges stay unsigned. Footnote markers are preserved in every quoted definition: a quote presented as verbatim that hides a definitional footnote inside itself is the exactness failure this corpus exists to report.

definitions.definition: A product that is all or virtually all made in the United States will ordinarily be one in which all significant parts <SUP>112</SUP> and processing that go into the product are of U.S. origin. In other words, where a product is labeled or otherwise advertised with an unqualified ``Made in USA'' claim, it should contain only a de minimis, or negligible, amount of foreign content.
definitions.character: enforcement policy, not codified rule text — it states how the Commission will exercise its enforcement discretion

resolves_onward_to.why: the statement makes the last substantial transformation a prerequisite, and takes the term as the Customs Service uses it — so the FTC's gloss of an unsigned term bottoms out in the same case-law term Part 134 uses twice and never defines
resolves_onward_to.quote: in order to be considered all or virtually all made in the United States, it is a prerequisite that the product have been last ``substantially transformed'' in the United States, as that term is used by the U.S. Customs Service `` i.e., the product should not be required to be marked ``made in [foreign country]'' under 19 U.S.C. 1304.<SUP>113</SUP>

definitions.definition: The word ``parts'' is used in its general sense throughout this enforcement policy statement to refer to all physical inputs into a product, including but not limited to subassemblies, components, parts, or materials.
definitions.character: footnote 112, definitional for the whole policy statement. It sits inside the sentence that glosses 'all or virtually all', next to § 323.2's own unsigned 'ingredients or components'
